> §43 successor-remediation skeleton. Companion to `material_catalog_admin.md` (the material
> TYPE vocabulary) — this covers the per-job **expected materials**, their scheduled loads, and
> the delivery ledger. The polished §6a operator guide lands with the enablement-doc program.

## What it is

The **Materials tracking** page (`/jobs/<job id>/materials`) is where a job's expected materials
live. It is reached by deep link only — there is no home card, because the page is job-scoped:

- from the **Job Tracker** → a job's detail → *Materials tracking →*
- from **My Tasks → Daily report** → the *Expected materials* card → *Materials tracking →*

The daily report itself shows **counts only** — how many lines are on the list, how many are still
expected, how many are flagged. Its per-line *Confirm receipt* and *Report a problem* buttons were
removed on 2026-08-11 (#74); every mark is made on the Materials tracking page.

It is a portal surface: D1 only, no send, no AI. Everything is capability-gated server-side; the
buttons the page shows are affordances, not the boundary.

| Who | What they can do |
|---|---|
| **Admin** (`cap.materials.manage`; **Manager too once migration 0079 is applied** — check `role_capabilities` for the live holder set) | Author the expected list — description or catalog type, part number, category, qty/unit, expected **ship** and **delivery** dates — plus the scheduled **loads** under each line. Also everything a manager can do. |
| **Manager** (`cap.materials.receive` + a manager/admin role) | Mark each line **Delivered / Partially delivered / Not delivered**, each with an optional note and load reference. A **quantity is REQUIRED** on Delivered and Partially delivered, and refused on Not delivered (2026-08-24). **Void** a mistaken mark and record the correct entry in its place (migration 0080 — see [Voiding a mistaken delivery mark](#voiding-a-mistaken-delivery-mark)), including a mark on a line already removed from the list (void only — see [Removing a line](#removing-a-line-and-the-removed-from-the-list-group)). |
| **Field PM / submitter** | Read the list for the job they are placed on. No marking, no voiding, no editing. A voided entry shows them **that** it was voided, but not who voided it or why. |

### The one idea worth understanding: marks are a LEDGER, not a flag

A part number routinely arrives across several truckloads. So a delivery mark **appends an event**
(`material_receipt_events`) rather than flipping a switch, and the line's displayed state is a
**rollup** over those events:

- the pill shows the **latest** mark that still counts; the running total is the **sum** of the
  quantities of every mark that still counts
- **marking the same line again is normal and expected** — partial, partial, then delivered
- a mark is **never deleted and never edited**. A mistaken one is **voided**: it stays in the line's
  history, struck through and labelled with who voided it, when, and why, and it stops counting
  toward every total on every surface. If the mark was wrong rather than a duplicate, the correct
  entry is then recorded as a new mark linked to the voided one. A void cannot be undone.
- a line that still has deliveries that count **cannot be removed** from the list — void them
  first. A removed line's deliveries would otherwise keep counting where nobody can see them.

Two states sit on **different axes** and must not be confused:

- the **delivery rollup** (not marked / partial / delivered / not delivered) — from the ledger
- the **problem flag** (`incident`) — set by *Report a problem* (on this page since 2026-08-11; the
  daily form carried it before). It is **sticky**:
  recording a later delivery against a flagged line **records the delivery but does not clear the
  flag** — the running total and delivered quantity keep tracking the ledger while the flag stays —
  and every surface (page, daily form, the Material List sheet) keeps showing the problem.
  That is deliberate — a delivered-but-damaged pallet is still a problem.
- clearing the flag is an **explicit human act**: the **Resolve problem** button beside the flag
  (manager/admin), with a required note saying how it was resolved. The line then lands where the
  delivery ledger says — *received* if the latest mark that still counts was a full delivery, back
  to *expected* otherwise — and the Material Incidents sheet's Line Status finally shows the
  resolution.

## Voiding a mistaken delivery mark

A double tap, a mark for a load that was already marked, or a quantity typo used to inflate the line
on every surface until someone edited the database by hand. Since migration 0080 the crew fixes it in
the portal. The fix is the job crew's or the office's own action; the Successor-Operator's part is to
point them at it and check the result landed.

**Who can void.** Exactly the people who can mark: a **manager placed on the job**, or an **admin on
any job**. A subcontractor (submitter) account cannot. Anyone who may void may void **anyone's** mark
— the mistake is usually someone else's double tap.

**Step one — void the wrong entry.**

1. Open the job's **Materials tracking** page and find the line. Its delivery history lists every
   mark with its quantity, note, date and who recorded it. Each entry also ends with the **time** it
   was recorded (Pacific, HH:MM), so two identical marks from a double tap can be told apart.
2. Tap **Void** beside the wrong entry. A panel opens explaining what a void does.
3. Type **why** it is being voided. The reason is required and is kept with the entry for good —
   "double tap", "same load as the 2026-03-14 mark", "qty typed as 400, was 40".
4. Tap **Confirm void**. The page says "Entry voided" and the line's total and pill update at once.

**Step two — say whether that was all.** Straight after a void the page asks which it was:

- **Done — it was a duplicate** (listed first; the usual case). Voiding it was the whole fix.
- **Record the correct entry** — only when the mark was *wrong* rather than a duplicate. A panel
  opens, filled in from the voided entry, with labelled **Kind**, **Qty**, **Note**, **Date** and
  **Load** fields, and the line's voided entries are shown so the one being replaced stays in view.
  Change what was wrong (usually the quantity or the kind) and record it.

**About a correct entry.**

- The correct entry shows a **Corrects …** tag naming the voided entry's date, kind and quantity;
  the voided one shows **Corrected by …** naming the correction's.
- It takes the voided entry's **place** in the history. A fix recorded weeks later, after other
  deliveries landed, does not become "the latest thing the field told us", so it does not flip the
  line's status back.
- There is **no time limit**. A quieter **Record the correct entry** button stays beside any voided
  entry that has no correction yet, so coming back next week works.
- A correction needs the line to still be **on the list**. A line already removed is void-only —
  see [Removing a line](#removing-a-line-and-the-removed-from-the-list-group).
- Each voided entry can be corrected **once**. If the correction itself was wrong, void the
  correction and record the right entry against it.
- If a good mark was voided by mistake, record the correct entry against it with the original values.
  That puts the count back, in the same place in the history.

**Show voided.** Voided entries are hidden from a line's history by default. A **Show voided (N)**
button under the history says how many are hidden; tap it to see them struck through with their
**Voided** tag and the "by … on … — reason" line (the date written YYYY-MM-DD, like the entry
dates). A subcontractor (submitter) account sees the **Voided** tag but not who voided it or why.

**What changes where.**

| Surface | What a void does |
|---|---|
| The Materials tracking page | The total and the pill drop the voided mark straight away |
| The daily report's Expected materials card | Shows counts only (lines, still expected, flagged). A void that takes a line back to *expected* shows in the "still expected" count the next time the form loads |
| The job's **Material List** Smartsheet | `Delivered Qty` and `Status` follow on the next sync cycle (about 90 seconds) while the materials mirror is on. `Received At` / `Received By` go back to the latest mark that still counts (blank when none is left) — never to the person who voided. If the line's `Note` was the voided mark's note, it goes back to the latest counting mark's note (blank when none has one) — flagged lines included. A line with a problem flag keeps its flag and its received stamp. Recording a correct entry in an earlier entry's place does not re-stamp `Received At` / `Received By` either; only a mark that lands as the line's latest does |
| The job's **Material Receipts** Smartsheet | The row is **kept, never deleted**. On the next sync cycle it reads `Entry Status = Voided`, turns gray, and fills `Voided By`, `Voided At` and `Void Reason`. `Line Qty Received` drops the voided quantity on every row for that line. A correct entry arrives as a new row whose `Supersedes` names the voided row's Event UUID; the voided row's `Superseded By` names the correction's |
| The **Weekly Production Report** (page 5 delivery log) | The voided mark drops off the next compile, and a correct entry prints on its own date. If the office **curated** that week's delivery list, a curated row copied from the voided mark is handled when the report is read: when its correct entry is a counting *Delivered* / *Partially delivered* mark dated inside that same week (and not already on the list), the correct entry **takes the row's place**; otherwise the row is **dropped**. A gold notice on the weekly report screen says how many rows were replaced and how many removed. Tick **Compile Now** to regenerate the PDF |
| A curated week saved **before** this change | Rows curated before migration 0080 carry no link back to their mark, so a later void cannot find them. The office taps **Remove** on that row on the weekly report screen, taps **Save weekly report inputs**, then ticks **Compile Now** |
| A report already compiled and **sent** | Unchanged. A sent PDF is a record of what the client received — see the escalation list |
| Photos already attached to the voided delivery | Left alone. A **new** photo cannot be attached to a voided mark ("That delivery record isn't on this material line") — attach it to the correct entry instead |
| A mark on a line already **removed** from the list | See [Removing a line](#removing-a-line-and-the-removed-from-the-list-group): the Material Receipts sheet and the weekly report follow as above; the Material List row does not change |

**The "already fully received" question.** Marking **Delivered** or **Partially delivered** on a
line that already has its full quantity received asks first: "This line already has 40 of 40 ea
received. Record another delivery anyway?" with **Record another delivery** and **Cancel**. It is the
cheapest place to stop a double mark before it needs voiding. The same question appears inside the
correction panel when the line is still fully received after the void, ending "Record the correction
anyway?" instead.

## Removing a line, and the "Removed from the list" group

**A line that still has deliveries that count cannot be removed.** **Remove** on it is refused
with "This line has deliveries recorded. Void them first, then remove the line."
(`line_has_deliveries`). A removed line drops off this page's list and the Material List sheet, but
its deliveries would keep counting on the Material Receipts sheet and the weekly report — a delivery
nobody could see or fix. So: if the deliveries really were mistakes, void each one (step one above),
then remove the line. A line whose deliveries are **all voided** can be removed; its scheduled loads
go with it, as before. If the deliveries are real, the line is not finished with — leave it on the
list.

**The "Removed from the list" group.** Every removed line that has any delivery history is listed in
a separate **Removed from the list** group on the page, each with "Removed from this job's list.
Deliveries recorded against it still count until voided." and its history. **Lines removed before
this rule** may still carry deliveries that count — those are the ones that matter. A line removed
after its deliveries were voided shows there too, with nothing left counting.

- A manager placed on the job, or an admin, can **Void** a delivery there exactly as above.
- Nothing else: there is no mark button and no **Record the correct entry** on a removed line. If a
  delivery belongs to a line still on the list, void it here and mark it on that line.
- A void there drops the delivery from the Material Receipts sheet's `Line Qty Received` and from the
  weekly report, on the next sync cycle and compile. The **Material List** row for a removed line
  reads `On List = Removed` and is no longer updated, so it keeps the totals it had when the line was
  removed.
- Whether those old deliveries are real is the office's call, not the Successor-Operator's. Point
  the office at the group; do not void on anyone's behalf.

## Activation order (Seth)

A deploy is high-class (a code change): this section is for the Developer-Operator.

Voiding, the removal refusal and the **Removed from the list** group arrive in one portal deploy
that reads columns migration **0080** adds. The database migration must land **before** the Worker:
a Worker deployed ahead of it fails Materials page loads and marks until the migration is applied.
The order, run by Seth from `safety_portal/` (full steps and the migration table in
`safety_portal/README.md`):

1. `git pull origin main` — never deploy or migrate from a stale checkout.
2. Apply the D1 migrations to the **remote** database.
3. `npm run deploy` — never a bare `wrangler deploy`, which can ship a stale page bundle.

The Material Receipts sheet's six void columns arrive with the Mac-side code: they are added to each
job's sheet on the first sync cycle after the production tree pulls main (see
[fieldops_sync.md](fieldops_sync.md) Symptom G). The Successor-Operator runs none of these steps.

## Symptoms

| Symptom | What it means | What the Successor-Operator does |
|---|---|---|
| A manager has no **Delivered / Partially delivered / Not delivered** buttons | Marking needs `cap.materials.receive` **and** a manager/admin role. A submitter holds the capability but not the role — by design, the same gate the daily report uses | Check the account's role in **Accounts**. If they should be marking deliveries, they need the manager role — not a new capability |
| "You're not assigned to that job" (403 `forbidden_job`) | Non-admins only reach the job they are **placed on** (`personnel.current_job`) | Place them on the job via **Personnel** / the job's crew. This is the designed scope, not a fault |
| The *Materials tracking →* button is missing from the job page or the daily report | The account lacks `cap.materials.receive` | Confirm the role in **Accounts**. All three roles normally hold it |
| The page says "Nothing is on this job's materials list yet" | No expected lines have been authored for the job | Not a fault. The office (admin) adds them on this page — or uploads the vendor's BOM through **Import a manifest** and commits the accepted lines from the validate screen (`material_manifest_import.md`) |
| "Could not load this job's materials" | Transient read failure — the page says so and offers **Retry** rather than showing an empty list | Tap **Retry**. If persistent, check whether the job's detail page loads at all, then escalate. If it started right after a portal deploy, the deploy may have gone out before its database migration (see [Activation order](#activation-order-seth)) — escalate |
| A line shows the **wrong running total** | The total is the SUM of the quantities of every mark that still counts. A duplicate mark contributes twice. Events recorded **before 2026-08-24** may carry no quantity at all and contribute nothing — quantity only became mandatory on that date, so an old green *Delivered* line can still read as fully outstanding | Open the line's history — every mark shows its quantity, note, date and who recorded it. A duplicate: have a manager on the job (or an admin) **Void** it. A mark with the wrong or a missing quantity: **Void** it, then **Record the correct entry** with the real quantity (see [Voiding a mistaken delivery mark](#voiding-a-mistaken-delivery-mark)). The real quantities come from the crew or the office, never from a guess |
| A line still shows **Problem reported** after the goods arrived | Working as designed — the incident flag is sticky and a delivery mark does not clear it | Not a fault. The delivery IS recorded (check the history and the running total — both keep moving). When the problem is genuinely settled, a manager/admin taps **Resolve problem** beside the flag and writes how it was resolved — that is the one thing that clears it |
| "Add a note explaining the shortfall" when marking **Not delivered** | A non-delivery must say why — the note is required, and a quantity is refused on it | Add the note. If a quantity genuinely arrived, the mark is *Partially delivered*, not *Not delivered* |
| "Enter the quantity received before recording this delivery" (red, beside the Qty box) | Working as designed since 2026-08-24. A Delivered or Partially delivered mark must say HOW MUCH arrived, or it cannot move the line's outstanding balance — the page refuses to arm the button until the box is filled | Type the quantity that actually arrived and tap again. If nothing arrived, the mark is **Not delivered**, which takes a note instead and no quantity |
| "That load isn't on this material line" | The chosen load belongs to a different line | Pick one of that line's own loads, or leave the load blank — the mark records fine without one |
| A load can't be removed / a line can't be edited | Line editing needs `cap.materials.manage` (admin; manager too once migration 0079 is applied), and a line that has been received or flagged is a **record** — content edits are locked (`not_editable`) | Expected. If the record itself is wrong, escalate |
| The daily report's *Expected materials* has no **Confirm receipt** or per-line buttons | Working as designed since 2026-08-11 (#74). The daily report shows counts only — lines on the list, still expected, flagged — and a **Materials tracking →** button | Not a fault. Every mark is made on the Materials tracking page |
| Tapping **Delivered / Partially delivered / Not delivered** records nothing the first time | Working as designed. A mark is permanent — a mistaken one can be voided, but only once someone notices, and until then every total reads wrong — so the buttons are two-step: the first tap ARMS the button (its label changes to "Confirm delivered?") and the second records it | Tap it again to confirm. Changed your mind? Tap a different button — that re-arms the new one and never records the first |
| "This line already has 40 of 40 ea received. Record another delivery anyway?" | Working as designed. The line already has its full quantity received, so another Delivered or Partially delivered mark would put it over. This is the usual way a double mark starts | If a further load really did arrive (an over-delivery, a replacement), tap **Record another delivery**. If not, tap **Cancel** — nothing is recorded. If an earlier mark is the wrong one, void that instead |
| A button that said "Confirm …?" reverted to its normal label on its own | Arming expires after a few seconds, so a button left armed cannot be committed minutes later by a stray tap | Not a fault. Tap twice again |
| A delivery photo won't attach — "that material line isn't on this job any more" | The photo's line binding is checked against the job's ACTIVE lines at UPLOAD, on purpose: the binding can't be accepted from the submission body, or a photo could be pointed at any line by editing the payload | Refresh the materials page so the line list is current, then attach the photo again. If the line really was removed, the photo can still be filed as an ordinary day photo |
| A delivery got recorded by mistake anyway | Marks are never deleted, but a mistaken one can be **voided** (since migration 0080) | A manager placed on the job, or an admin, opens the line's history, taps **Void** beside the wrong entry, types why, and taps **Confirm void**. If the mark was wrong rather than a duplicate, they then **Record the correct entry**. Check the line's total on the page, and the sheets after one sync cycle. See [Voiding a mistaken delivery mark](#voiding-a-mistaken-delivery-mark) |
| There is no **Void** button beside an entry | Either the account cannot mark on this job (the same role and placement rules as marking — see the first two rows), or the entry is already voided (it shows a red **Voided** tag) | Fix the role or placement as for marking. An already-voided entry offers **Record the correct entry** instead, until it has one (on a line still on the list) |
| A voided entry shows **Voided** but no name or reason | The account is a subcontractor (submitter). By design they see that an entry was voided, not who voided it or why | Not a fault. A manager or admin sees the full "by … on … — reason" line |
| A voided entry has disappeared from the history | Voided entries are hidden by default | Tap **Show voided (N)** under the line's history. Nothing was deleted |
| "Say why this entry is being voided — the reason is kept with it." (`reason_required`) | The reason box was left empty — a void must say why | Type the reason and tap **Confirm void** again |
| "The reason must be plain text, up to 500 characters." (`invalid_reason`) | The reason is too long | Shorten it to a sentence or two and confirm again |
| "That entry was already voided — refresh to see who voided it and why." (`already_voided`) | Someone else voided the same entry first, or the first tap of a double tap already landed. Only one void is ever recorded | Refresh the page. Nothing more to do unless the entry also needs a correct entry recorded |
| "That job is no longer active, so its delivery history can't be changed." (`job_not_active`) | The job was closed or archived. A closed job's delivery history is frozen on purpose — its sheets have moved to the archive | Refused by design. If the closed job's history really must change, escalate |
| "Only a voided entry can be corrected — void the wrong entry first, then record the correct one." (`supersedes_not_voided`) | A correct entry can only replace a voided one | Void the wrong entry first, then use **Record the correct entry** on it |
| "That voided entry already has a correction — refresh to see it." (`already_corrected`) | Each voided entry can be corrected once, and this one already was (often by a colleague at the same moment) | Refresh and read the correction. If the correction is itself wrong, void the correction and record the right entry against it |
| "The entry being corrected isn't on this material line any more — refresh to see the history." (`unknown_supersedes`) | The page was out of date — the entry being corrected is not on this line | Refresh the page and start the correction again from the voided entry's own **Record the correct entry** button. If it keeps happening, escalate |
| "The entry being corrected couldn't be identified — refresh to see the history." (`invalid_supersedes_id`) | The page sent a broken reference — a stale or damaged page, not something the person did | Refresh and try again from the voided entry. If it keeps happening, escalate |
| The Material Receipts sheet still shows a voided delivery | Working as designed. The sheet keeps every mark; a voided one stays, grayed, with `Entry Status = Voided` and who/when/why filled in | Not a fault. Read `Entry Status`, not just the row's presence. Totals on the sheet (`Line Qty Received`) already leave it out |
| The Material Receipts sheet does not show a void yet | The sheet follows on the next sync cycle (about 90 seconds), and only while the receipts mirror is on | Wait a cycle or two. Then check `field_ops.fieldops_sync.receipts_enabled` in ITS_Config and the receipts-mirror symptoms in [fieldops_sync.md](fieldops_sync.md) Symptom G. Still missing after several cycles with `fieldops_sync` errors in `ITS_Errors` — escalate |
| One job's Material Receipts sheet has stopped updating, and `ITS_Errors` shows `material_receipts_column_backfill_failed` for it | The mirror cannot add the six void columns to that sheet, so it pauses that job's receipts rows until it can. Other jobs carry on, and nothing is lost | Follow [fieldops_sync.md](fieldops_sync.md) Symptom G for that code: wait a cycle or two, check the circuit breaker and the `fieldops_sync` heartbeat, escalate if it persists or names a permission refusal |
| Six new columns (`Entry Status` … `Superseded By`) appeared at the far right of a Material Receipts sheet | `material_receipts_columns_backfilled` — a sheet created before migration 0080 was brought up to date, once | Not a fault. Drag the columns if you prefer them elsewhere |
| The weekly report screen shows a gold notice — "1 delivery row was replaced with the corrected entry." and/or "2 delivery rows were removed because their marks were voided." (the numbers vary) | Working as designed. The office curated that week's delivery list, and one or more of those rows came from a mark that has since been voided. Where the correct entry is a delivery dated inside the same week, it took the row's place; otherwise the row is left off the client's report | Not a fault — the notice is informational. Tick **Compile Now** on the week sheet so the PDF matches. If the week's report was already sent, see the escalation list |
| A voided delivery still prints on a curated week of the Weekly Production Report | The row was curated **before** migration 0080 and carries no link back to its mark, so the void cannot find it | Open that week on the weekly report screen, **Remove** the row, tap **Save weekly report inputs**, then tick **Compile Now** |
| "This line has deliveries recorded. Void them first, then remove the line." (`line_has_deliveries`) | A line with deliveries that still count cannot be removed — its deliveries would keep counting where nobody can see them | If the deliveries were mistakes, void each one, then remove the line. If they are real, the line stays on the list. See [Removing a line](#removing-a-line-and-the-removed-from-the-list-group) |
| A **Removed from the list** group appears on the Materials page | Removed lines that have delivery history — usually lines removed before the rule above, whose deliveries may still count. The group lists them with their history | Not a fault. The office decides whether those deliveries are real; a manager on the job (or an admin) can **Void** any that are not. The group has no mark or correction buttons by design |
| A job's **Material List** Smartsheet has no **Part Number / Category / Expected Ship Date** columns | The sheet was created before those columns existed. The mirror back-fills them automatically on its next cycle for that job — a sheet's columns are fixed at create, so pre-existing sheets are topped up rather than rebuilt | Wait one sync cycle and re-open the sheet. `ITS_Errors` records `material_list_columns_backfilled` naming exactly what was added. If instead you see `material_list_column_backfill_failed` repeatedly, the top-up cannot write — escalate |
| The new columns appear at the **far right**, not beside `Expected Date` | Deliberate. Back-filled columns can only be appended, so the creation schema appends them too — otherwise back-filled and newly-created sheets would show the same columns in a different order forever | Not a fault. Drag the columns in Smartsheet if you prefer them elsewhere; column order is display-only and the mirror does not depend on it |
| **Expected Date** and **Expected Ship Date** disagree | They are different dates by design — `Expected Date` is when the goods are expected to ARRIVE, `Expected Ship Date` is when they LEAVE | Not a fault. If one is wrong, correct it in the portal; the mirror is one-way-up and re-projects next cycle |

## Escalate to Seth (Developer-Operator) — high-capability-class

Voiding a mark and recording the correct entry are the crew's and office's own in-portal actions
(Tier-2: the Successor-Operator guides and checks). Escalate when what is asked for goes past them:

- **Un-voiding or deleting a mark.** A void is permanent and a mark is never deleted — there is no
  undo and none must be improvised in the database. (A good mark voided by mistake is fixed in the
  portal by recording the correct entry against it — see the voiding section.)
- **A void refused because the job is no longer active** ("That job is no longer active, so its
  delivery history can't be changed."). Refused by design; changing a closed or archived job's
  history is Seth's call.
- **A week whose report was already compiled and sent to the client.** The sent PDF is a record of
  what the client received — do not try to change it or re-send it. A void corrects the next
  compile; whether the client needs a corrected report is Seth's call.
- **The Material Receipts sheet still does not show a void after several sync cycles**, with
  `fieldops_sync` errors in `ITS_Errors`.
- **The Materials page fails to load, or marks fail, right after a portal deploy.** The deploy may
  have gone out before migration 0080 reached the database — see [Activation order](#activation-order-seth).
- **Restoring a removed line itself.** There is no in-portal un-remove. (Adding the material again as
  a new line is the office's own action and needs no escalation.)
- **Clearing a stuck `incident` flag** on a line.
- Anything touching the **§51 Material List Smartsheet mirror**, which is one-way-up permanently.
- **Data loss / restore.** `material_receipt_events` and `material_shipments` are **D1-primary**.
  Daily reports filed before 2026-08-11 also carry a materials snapshot in their filed PDF on Box
  (since then every mark is made on this page), and the coarse per-line state mirrors up to the
  Material List sheet when
  `field_ops.fieldops_sync.materials_enabled` is on — but the **per-event history of a mark made on
  this page** exists only in D1. The restore path is Cloudflare **D1 Time Travel** (30-day
  point-in-time restore of the whole database). See `docs/tech_debt.md` → "D1-primary tables have
  no ITS-side backup", whose revisit trigger this capability fired.
